data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Idempotency (f(f(x))=f(x)) is the property an append-only event log must require of its writers; safety is a weaker, orthogonal property about not corrupting other operations and is insufficient alone. The exact distinction: idempotency constrains an operation's effect on itself under repeated application, while safety constrains its effect on the outcomes of other operations during retry.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If 'safe' is defined in the cited literature to subsume idempotency (safe = idempotent + non-interfering), then safety would be the required property and idempotency alone would be insufficient.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log implements transparent deduplication via operation IDs before replay, neither property of the underlying operation is required \u2014 the log fabricates idempotency at the append layer.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the system uses exactly-once delivery (not at-least-once), neither property is strictly required since duplicates never occur.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"At-least-once delivery causally guarantees that a writer's operation will arrive at the log zero or more times, with at least one arrival. When a retried append creates a duplicate entry, the replay engine will apply the encoded operation multiple times. If the operation is idempotent, the causal chain is: duplicate application \u2192 same state transition \u2192 same final state. If the operation is merely safe (retry does not alter other operations' results), the duplicate application still produces a wrong result for THIS operation (e.g., a non-idempotent increment applied twice yields 2 instead of 1), even though no other operation is corrupted. Thus safety prevents collateral damage but permits self-damage; idempotency prevents self-damage, which is the actual failure mode of at-least-once replay.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
